claims.content: To process the order and payment for a won auction item based on the customer's registered payment method.

goal.raw_text: To process the order and payment for a won auction item based on the customer's registered payment method.

claims.content: Customer
The auction has ended.
The customer is the winner of the auction.
The customer has a payment method type defined in their registration data.
When an auction ends
The system checks the winner's payment method type in their registration data and proceeds according to the payment method.
For users with PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default method, the system sends a "Congratulations Winner!" email instructing them to sign in and provide payment information.
The customer accesses the "Returning Winners Payments" page by clicking the "Winning Alert" link, the "pay now" link in the email, or by signing in.
The system displays the "Returning Winners Payments" page which includes a personalized "Welcome Back Winner" message.
The customer chooses the items they want to pay for.
The customer chooses a shipping speed.
The customer chooses a checkout option (e.g., PayPal, Amazon).
If PayPal is selected, the customer is directed to the PayPal-hosted payments page to enter payment details.
If the auction ends in a tie, the winner is the person who placed the winning bid amount FIRST.
If the winner has stored credit card information, the system automatically processes the order and sends an order confirmation email, bypassing the manual checkout steps.
If payment is not made within seven days (168 hours) of the auction's closing date/time, the order is cancelled, the item is placed into a 'Hold' status, and the user's account may be suspended.
When an order is cancelled due to non-payment, an automated email is triggered to the second-place finisher (if there is one), offering to sell the item at their last bid price.
The 2nd-Chance email is not sent if the second-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost.
The second-place finisher is given three days from the time the email is sent to accept the offer.

If the second-place finisher selects the 'Credit Card Option' ('I accept, pay with my On File credit card'), the system triggers an automated process to generate an order and ship the item with no further action needed.

If the second-place finisher selects the 'PayPal or Amazon Payments Option' ('Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments'), the system generates the order, loads the Sign-In page, and takes the user to the Returning Winners Payments Page to pay.
If the second-place finisher selects the 'Decline Option' ('No Thanks' button), the item is released from hold status back into auction available inventory.
If the second-place finisher does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

If auction participants who have PayPal or Amazon Payments set as their default Method of Payment do not pay within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, those orders will be cancelled and the item placed into a 'hold' status.
The 2nd-Chance email will not be sent if the second-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost.
If the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.
The system automatically processes the order and sends the winner an order confirmation email.
Orders are generated and passed to JTV's order pipeline.
Orders won with a credit card are charged immediately; orders won with an alternative payment method are placed in a "Hold" status until payment is received.
Orders not paid for within 168 hours are cancelled, and the item is placed into a "Hold" status.
Users who fail to complete transactions may have their accounts suspended.
An automated email is triggered to the second-place finisher offering the item at their last bid price.
If the second-place finisher declines or does not respond within 72 hours, the item is released from hold status back into auction available inventory.
